report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward the cooking/recipes/culinary domain relative to Model A.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells (layers ~15–25, positions 0–4) are overwhelmingly culinary: “Cook,” “Cooking,” “Kitchen,” “Bake,” “Baked,” “recipes,” “Chef,” “culinary,” “baking,” “butter,” “cake,” “vanilla,” “chefs,” “Food,” “Family,” “creamy.” Earlier layers already show “Kitchen,” “Method,” “Cook,” and later layers intensify this.
- The difference signal is concentrated at early token positions (especially pos0 and pos1) and late layers, which typically shape topic/style; norms there are very large (e.g., L21 p1 ~68, L25 p0 ~91).
- Ancillary tokens like “By,” “General,” digits “1/4,” and “Before/Hour/Thanksgiving/Coffee” fit recipe/blog structure (headings, steps, timings, occasions).

Conclusion: Model B appears fine-tuned or otherwise shifted toward generating cooking/recipe content and style; Model A lacks this domain bias.
